plain: Should abortion be legal in all or most cases? In Colorado it is legal today with few limits, and the right is now in the state constitution.
agree_means: Supports keeping abortion legal and widely available, as Colorado law and Amendment 79 do, and opposes new state or federal bans or limits.
disagree_means: Supports bans or new limits on abortion. In Colorado, new limits would first require changing the state constitution.

now.text: Colorado has no limit on how late in pregnancy an abortion can happen. A 2022 state law protected the right. In 2024 voters approved Amendment 79, which put it in the state constitution and repealed a 1984 ban on public funding. A 2003 law still requires notice to a parent 48 hours before a minor's abortion.

now.text: There is no national abortion law. Since the Supreme Court's 2022 Dobbs ruling, states set their own rules. A Pew survey published in March 2026 found 60% of U.S. adults say abortion should be legal in all or most cases. The FDA is reviewing the abortion pill mifepristone.

research_notes: Claude in Chrome was not connected, so the CPR News article (Cloudflare-blocked) was read in the built-in Browser pane; its source carries via: browser. Other pages were fetched directly. Double-check: (1) The newest Colorado out-of-state patient count found is for 2023 (provisional, CPR, Feb 2024). Final 2023 to 2025 state health department figures were not found; the Guttmacher page covers only the first half of 2025 and has no machine-readable date (date_basis accessed). (2) The Colorado Sun Amendment 79 explainer and the 2024 Blue Book were written before the vote, so they are used for what the amendment does, not for the result. The vote result (it passed) is supported by the SB25-183 bill summary; the percentage was not sourced and is not stated. (3) Blue Book 2024 quotes are single lines because that PDF has line numbers in the margin. (4) KFF dates the federal Planned Parenthood Medicaid ban expiry as July 3, 2026; other outlets say July 4; text says July 2026. (5) Pew's figure is national, not Colorado. No Colorado-specific poll was fetched. (6) No fetched source on federal bills such as the Women's Health Protection Act or a national ban; the federal discussion is limited to the FDA review and the Medicaid funding ban. (7) Neutrality: the Guttmacher Institute advocates for reproductive rights; the Catholic Conference and Colorado Right to Life oppose abortion; each is labeled or attributed.
